title: region-aware reservation and heuristic spill smoother for KV cache
author: Marisol Vega
description: Problem: tail latency and memory fragmentation under multi-tenant workloads cause frequent spillovers to SSD even when global free memory exists. Small tenants and skewed hotspots starve large contiguous regions needed by some models, increasing kernel scheduling jitter and KV cache churn. Motivation: reduce unnecessary spill I/O, keep high-priority tenants (dedicated pools) responsive, and improve latency stability for long-context requests. Design summary: 1) region-aware reservation: introduce soft reservations per region (power-of-two region units) that prefer allocation of contiguous slots for large entries while remaining reclaimable under pressure. Reservations decay based on recent allocation success and are charged to tenant weight; low-priority partitions can be preempted via soft handoff windows. 2) heuristic spill smoother: a spill controller that converts bursty eviction spikes into paced spill operations using a moving-window histogram of spill candidates, adaptive backpressure to request paths, and a prioritized async writer that coalesces neighboring pages into single write ops. 3) fragmentation hinting: eviction policy incorporates fragmentation score (live-run-length, hole density) and will prefer compaction-friendly victims when fragmentation crosses threshold. 4) paging throttle: scheduler-level token bucket that prevents background spill workers from saturating NVMe during peak foreground latency; tokens are replenished based on latency SLO signals from the tracing pipeline. Implementation notes: - Core changes in server/kv/cache/{region_reservation.cpp,h} and server/kv/evictor/{spill_smoother.cpp,h,policy.cpp} - Small kernel-level alignment helpers in runtime/utils/alloc_helpers.h - Expose two config knobs in config/kv.yaml: region_reservation.enabled and spill_smoother.aggressiveness - Added integration tests and a new microbenchmark under perf/kv/bench_spill_smoother.cc Benchmarks: - End-to-end synthetic tenant mix (50 tenants, 70/30 hot/cold, 1M requests over 20 minutes) shows 2.2x reduction in spill write amplification and 18% median p90 reduction for long-context generation workloads compared to master. - Worst-case tenant isolation test improved tail-latency (p99) by 12% when a small tenant attempts to allocate many contiguous slots. Compatibility: fully backward compatible config defaults (both features off by default). Migration/rollout plan: feature-flagged release, enable in Canary 1 (single-region), observe NVMe write bytes and p99 latency for two weeks, then staged rollout. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: incorrect reservation accounting could cause priority inversion. Mitigation: soft handoff that allows immediate preemption and extensive unit tests. - Risk: spill smoother might starve background GC. Mitigation: token-bucket with floor replenishment and integration-level watchdog. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached (linear ENG-1289) - [x] Unit tests for reservation accounting - [x] Integration perf bench outputs included - [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults - [x] Documentation stub in docs/ops/kv-cache.md

Priya Raman (2024-09-15): Spill smoother looks promising but the initial design may defer too aggressively under sustained pressure. Can we add a floor to the spill rate tied to NVMe throughput?
Marisol Vega (2024-09-15): Added token-bucket floor (configurable) and a short-circuit path for emergency GC that bypasses smoothing when free-memory < critical threshold.

release_notes:
- Add region-aware soft reservations to improve allocation of contiguous KV slots and reduce fragmentation-induced spillover.
- Introduce heuristic spill smoother to pace and coalesce background spill writes, reducing write amplification and improving tail latency.
- New config knobs: region_reservation.enabled, spill_smoother.window_scale, spill_smoother.token_bucket_floor.
